config.title: Pull-to-Refresh Feed

intro.title: Pull-to-Refresh Feed
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a mobile feed page that users can pull down to refresh, loading new content. You will learn how to use the Ionic Refresher component to detect the pull gesture and trigger a data reload. The core programming concept involves handling asynchronous events to update your app's state and UI. You'll implement this using Angular's data binding and TypeScript within an Ionic + Capacitor project.
intro.usecase: Pull-to-refresh is a fundamental mobile interaction pattern that appears in countless real-world apps where users need fresh content. You'll find it in social media feeds like Instagram or Twitter, messaging apps like WhatsApp, email clients like Gmail, and news readers like Flipboard. This pattern allows users to manually trigger content updates with a natural pulling gesture, providing immediate feedback that data is being refreshed. As a mobile developer, implementing pull-to-refresh correctly ensures your app feels responsive and follows platform conventions that users already understand.

objectives: Apply Ionic's IonRefresher component to implement pull-to-refresh functionality in an Angular template.
Define a TypeScript method to handle the refresh event and trigger data reloading.
Use Angular's HttpClient to fetch updated data from a mock API endpoint.
Implement a loading state to control the visibility of the refresher component during data fetching.
Execute the refreshComplete() method to signal the end of the refresh operation.
Store fetched data in a component property to update the displayed feed items.
Utilize Angular's lifecycle hooks (ngOnInit) to load initial data when the component initializes.
Construct a mock API service with a simulated delay to demonstrate asynchronous data loading.
Control the refresher's visual feedback by managing its state through Ionic's RefresherEvent interface.
Access and display dynamic data in the template using Angular's *ngFor directive for list rendering.

steps.title: Import Angular core modules

steps.hint: Add the imports to the @Component decorator's imports array. This gives your component access to Angular's common directives and HTTP client functionality.

steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported both CommonModule from '@angular/common' and HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http' in the imports array.

steps.title: Create the main component

steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. Make sure to set standalone: true.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a FeedPage component defined with the proper Angular component structure.
successCriteria: The component must be named FeedPage, use the @Component decorator, have selector 'app-feed', and set standalone: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the FeedPage component with the correct Angular structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you've included all required parts: component name FeedPage, @Component decorator, selector 'app-feed', and standalone: true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Make sure you're using the @Component decorator with the correct configuration.

steps.title: Set up component imports
steps.instruction: Add an imports array to the @Component decorator with the following modules: IonContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonRefresher, IonRefresherContent, CommonModule, and HttpClientModule.
steps.hint: The imports array goes inside the @Component decorator. You need to import these from the appropriate packages (Ionic components from '@ionic/angular', CommonModule from '@angular/common', HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http').
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's @Component decorator now includes an imports array with the specified Ionic components and Angular modules.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator should have an imports property containing an array with IonContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonRefresher, IonRefresherContent, CommonModule, and HttpClientModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the imports array to the component decorator. This makes the Ionic components and Angular modules available for use in your template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an imports array, but it's missing some required items. Make sure to include all of these: IonContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonRefresher, IonRefresherContent, CommonModule, and HttpClientModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports array wasn't added correctly. Remember to add an imports property to the @Component decorator with an array containing the specified Ionic components and Angular modules.

steps.title: Define the feed data interface
steps.instruction: Inside the FeedPage class, define a TypeScript interface named FeedItem with three properties: id of type number, title of type string, and content of type string.
steps.hint: Add an interface declaration above the FeedPage class. Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a FeedItem interface that defines the structure of feed data items with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The interface should be named FeedItem and include exactly three typed properties: id: number, title: string, and content: string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the FeedItem interface with proper TypeScript types. This will ensure type safety when working with feed data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface has all three required properties with the correct TypeScript types: id (number), title (string), and content (string).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Make sure you're defining an interface named FeedItem with id: number, title: string, and content: string properties.

steps.title: Initialize feed data state
steps.instruction: Inside the FeedPage component class, add a property named feedItems with the type FeedItem[] and initialize it with an array containing at least two sample feed items.
steps.hint: Declare a property in the class body using TypeScript syntax: feedItems: FeedItem[] = []; then populate the array with objects matching your FeedItem interface structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a feedItems property initialized with sample data that can be displayed in the template.
successCriteria: The FeedPage class contains a feedItems property of type FeedItem[] that is initialized with an array of at least two objects matching the FeedItem interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the feed data state with sample items. This gives us data to work with in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure feedItems is declared as a property in the FeedPage class with the correct type FeedItem[], and it's initialized with at least two sample objects that match your FeedItem interface structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The feedItems property isn't properly initialized. Check that you've added it to the FeedPage class with the correct type annotation and populated it with sample data objects.

steps.title: Define the refresh handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the FeedPage component class, add a method named handleRefresh that takes an event parameter and returns a Promise<void>. The method should be async and for now just log 'Refreshing...' to the console.
steps.hint: Create an async method with the signature handleRefresh(event: any): Promise<void> { ... } inside the FeedPage class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeedPage component now has a handleRefresh method that can be called when the user performs a pull-to-refresh action.
successCriteria: The method should be named handleRefresh, be async, accept an event parameter, return Promise<void>, and log 'Refreshing...' to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the refresh handler method. This method will be triggered when the user pulls down to refresh the feed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your method is async, accepts an event parameter, returns Promise<void>, and logs 'Refreshing...' to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that you've created an async method named handleRefresh with the correct signature and console log.

steps.title: Implement refresh logic
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRefresh method, implement the refresh logic: use setTimeout to simulate a 2-second API delay,
steps.hint: Use setTimeout with an arrow function. Inside, create new feed items with unique IDs and add them to the beginning of the array using unshift(). Don't forget to call event.target.complete() after updating the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRefresh method will now properly simulate an API call with a delay, add new feed items to the beginning of the array, and complete the refresh event.
successCriteria: The handleRefresh method should contain: 1) setTimeout with 2000ms delay, 2) Creation of new FeedItem objects added to feedItems array using unshift(), 3) event.target.complete() call inside the setTimeout callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the refresh logic with proper delay simulation and array update.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check if you have all required elements: setTimeout with 2000ms, adding new items to feedItems array, and calling event.target.complete().
steps.feedbackWrong: The refresh logic implementation is incomplete or incorrect. Make sure to use setTimeout, add new items to the feedItems array, and complete the refresh event.

steps.title: Create the feed list
steps.instruction: After the IonRefresher component in your template, add an IonList that uses *ngFor to iterate through the feedItems array and display each item in an IonItem with an IonLabel.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic list components: IonList, IonItem, and IonLabel. Bind *ngFor to feedItems and display the item's title property in the IonLabel.

<ion-list>
  <ion-item *ngFor="let item of items">
    <ion-label>{{ item.name }}</ion-label>
  </ion-item>
</ion-list>
